_source: Generated by tools/gen_world_data.py from docs/world/*.md: edit the docs, not this file.
_doc: Night City's districts (World.district / World.districts), from the Night City 2045 sourcebook: manager, population, Security Code (n: faction, intensity, hardened), Utility Code, provider, gang influence, NCART stations, the neighbourhood generator profile, look tags, history, cite. Generated from docs/world/city.md and docs/world/nc_*.md.

charter_hill.name: Charter Hill
charter_hill.population: up-and-coming management-track execs and their families; menial staff are bussed in daily
look: view of the Exec Zone walls
charter_hill.history: Carved out of New Westbrook over the last decade by the merely wealthy; the new City Manager imports labour through a firm he part-owns.

downtown.name: Downtown
downtown.population: old post-nuke working families running small shops and repair joints, squeezed by Chamber-backed newcomers opening clinics, designer stores and bodysculpt shops
downtown.history: Once elegant West Hill Gardens; folded into Little Europe after the 4CW, then carved out as its own district in 2042 when the Chamber of Commerce bought a Council seat after years of squeezing supplies; Continental Plaza broke ground the next day.

executive_zone.name: Executive Zone
executive_zone.population: under 100 permanent residents, plus tracked day labourers and live-in servants
executive_zone.history: A walled enclave run by its Home Owners' Association; the HOA president sits as City Manager and the last election was won by one vote.

heywood_docks.name: Heywood Docks
heywood_docks.population: the smallest outside the Executive Zone; little housing, most dockers commute from North Heywood or New Westbrook
heywood_docks.history: Built by the Skiv Family with money from the Arroyo Concern corps and shipper DT&R, to undercut the nomad-run Port of Night City.

heywood_industrial_zone.name: Heywood Industrial Zone
heywood_industrial_zone.population: few residents: most workers commute; Zhirafa housing, a few container communities, contract Techs and teenage bike couriers
ncart: Industrial Zone Station (Red and Green Lines)
heywood_industrial_zone.history: Created after the 4th Corporate War by the Arroyo Concern (Militech, Petrochem, Raven, SovOil, Trauma Team) as a regional manufacturing hub; this year a start-up's hostile takeover of the couriers' ship briefly paralysed city deliveries.

hot_zone.name: The Hot Zone
hot_zone.population: hundreds, maybe thousands, none by choice: refugees, scavvers, streetrats and the desperate, plus gangers and worse who like it there
hot_zone.history: The old corporate centre, wrecked by the nuke in the 4th Corporate War; shrinking each year as Night Corp-funded nomad crews rebuild inward from The Glen, Little Europe and the Upper Marina, while Maelstrom, scavvers and Reckoners sabotage the reclamation.

kabuki.name: Kabuki
kabuki.population: overwhelmingly Japanese-descended refugees from Japantown and their children; a third have never lived anywhere else
kabuki.history: Founded by kabuki star Shinobu Nakagawa for Japantown refugees after the nuke, with NCCS corps and the Tyger Claws as patrons; his death in 2042 set off the bloody War of Succession.

little_china.name: Little China
little_china.population: north and centre ~50% ethnic Chinese, ~35% other Asian ancestry, ~15% other; LCRA aid favours Chinese residents, and those pushed out drift south to the Legion
little_china.history: Parts of old Charter Hill and Studio City were annexed after Ling Po bought the council seat; the LCRA rebuilds the north while the south stays a combat zone.

little_europe.name: Little Europe
little_europe.population: mostly working class, barely covering rent; artists, mercs, suits and blue-collar workers; home of Night Corp and Danger Gal HQs
little_europe.history: Stitched together after the 4CW from Little Italy, Northside and part of West Hill; Downtown split off in 2042 and the border is redrawn every year; a synthcoke gift-box bomb in a day market set off the Bozo Civil War.

new_westbrook.name: New Westbrook
new_westbrook.population: thousands, never counted; SIN-holding citizens are a small fraction, most residents are SINless after the DataKrash or born without one
new_westbrook.history: A suburb turned into a refugee camp by the 4th Corporate War and left that way for a generation; Network 54 and WorldSat took the hills for their transmitters and now keep it quiet.

norcal_military_base.name: NorCal Military Base
norcal_military_base.population: almost all COG soldiers, sailors and airmen; civilians who move on base must enlist in the COG Reserve; Militech staff live on site
norcal_military_base.history: Founded by the 2016 treaty that freed NorCal; its units besieged Night City in the 4th Corporate War, then in 2027 swore to NorCal as the Estero Bay Military COG.

north_heywood.name: North Heywood
north_heywood.population: working-class corp drones, junior Techs and dock and factory hands, plenty of ex-military; the poorest in cube hotels and container housing
north_heywood.history: Split from Heywood in 2038, leaving Santo Domingo as the other half; last year rising Inquisitor and Toecutter attacks pushed the City Manager to deputize 6th Street.

old_combat_zone.name: Old Combat Zone
old_combat_zone.population: split by generation: the older Faded (mostly in the Warren) and the younger ERI
old_combat_zone.history: The San Morro Industrial Zone was wrecked in the 4CW, resettled by Lasky's Faded, and made a district when Brick Coleman bought a Council seat in 2042.

old_japantown.name: Old Japantown
old_japantown.population: a core of residents of Japanese descent, increasingly mixed with gangers and Glen workers who can't afford The Glen
old_japantown.history: Wrecked by ground liquefaction and fallout from the 2023 nuke and abandoned for Kabuki; Sanroo later bought the district's government.

outskirts.name: The Outskirts
outskirts.population: Reclaimers, hermits, farmers and stubborn independents by choice, plus corporate company towns and passing nomads
outskirts.history: Lush land turned desert since the Collapse; locals care more about gossip than Raffen Shiv raids or the airport's crashes.

pacifica_playground.name: Pacifica Playground
pacifica_playground.population: Workers for Playland, Tanson, the Jodes and the vice trade; tourists nearly match residents at peak; Korean enclave around Tanson, Jodes nomads on the south edge
ncart: Orange Line station (unnamed on the map)
pacifica_playground.history: Playland reopened in 2036, Tanson moved in in 2040 and the Jodes camped here in 2041; Militech was hired this year when NCPD could not stop the Piranha-Voodoo Boys war.

playland.name: Playland by the Sea
playland.population: Tourists day and night, overworked park staff (about half Piranhas) and runaway kids living in yogangs in the park's hidden corners
playland.history: Reopened in 2036 under Tower of Dark; two years ago Bozos slipped through the Haunted Woods' drone blind spots and killed 30+ staff, hushed up with payments to Net54 and WNS.

port_of_night_city.name: Port of Night City
port_of_night_city.population: working class: young Thelas on rotation, old Night City locals, Russian transplants; Flotsam turns over constantly
port_of_night_city.history: The Thelas rebuilt and took over the Port after the 4th Corporate War; it split from South Night City in 2036 and now fends off corp pressure.

rancho_coronado.name: Rancho Coronado
rancho_coronado.population: War survivors of every background mixed with refugees, stuck and fending for themselves
rancho_coronado.history: Wrecked in the 4th Corporate War; leaderless since its cult-leader City Manager died in a 2037 bombing, now a static churn of gang scraps and drive-by raids.

reclamation_zone.name: Reclamation Zone
reclamation_zone.population: mostly the Dorado Clan (several families, about half Muslim); about 10% later joiners: NCART staff, prior locals, ex-nomads
reclamation_zone.history: Santos Dorado traded NCART upkeep for land; the Council split it off South Night City by a slim vote in 2039.

santo_domingo.name: Santo Domingo
santo_domingo.population: Mostly Latino/Hispanic working families making do on day work, plus nomads cycling through the Aldecaldo Camp
ncart: Green Line station (unnamed on the map)
santo_domingo.history: Split from Heywood, ran under Aldecaldo-backed managers for three terms, then fell to El Norte's candidate Theresa Valentino last year.

south_night_city.name: South Night City
south_night_city.population: large and diverse; the down-on-their-luck, pushed there or kept there by the system
south_night_city.history: Haakensen fled the nuke, bought the manager seat a decade later, then lost the Port and Reclamation Zone; a Zoner march on The Glen ended in deaths.

the_glen.name: The Glen
the_glen.population: very multicultural; mostly corpzoners and government employees, a district built for steady earners
the_glen.history: Built by Night Corp and its allies after the war on half of old South Night City to hold the new government; the Night Corp board appointed its City Manager last year.

university_district.name: University District
university_district.population: NCU students and faculty around the walled campus, professors in brick houses further out, Biotechnica scientists and staff in the east; most support workers commute in
university_district.history: The Dean used NCU's endowment to buy the council seat and fortified the campus through the war, then traded Biotechnica board seats and an HQ site for cash.

upper_marina.name: Upper Marina
upper_marina.population: stratified: yacht-owning rich in pieds-a-terre at the top, service and construction workers struggling with rent below
upper_marina.history: Pitched as Richard Night's bohemian waterfront; Chung's staff sell approvals for quick-build projects that rot, then pocket commissions reselling the land, and two new towers had to be demolished when their concrete dissolved in blood rain.

watson_development.name: Watson Development
watson_development.population: young and fast-growing: Night City locals, Pacifica job-seekers, Asian immigrants brought in by the NCCS and settled ex-nomads; the city's highest birth rate
watson_development.history: Raised on the ruins of North Oak and old Westbrook with NCCS money; last year a three-day district-wide strike forced open elections that swept organiser Lucius Rhyne in as City Manager.
